company: Prosus N.V. (forced seller of Delivery H
bull_thesis: The bull case is that the event resolved well and the market has not paid for what is left. Prosus, the Amsterdam-listed technology holding company, was ordered by Europe's competition regulator to shrink its 26.5% stake in Delivery Hero, the German food-delivery group, as the price of being allowed to buy Just Eat Takeaway.com. Management executed that mandated sale about as well as a forced sale can be executed: 4.5% to Uber at 20 euros a share on 17 April 2026, then 5% to Aspex Management of Hong Kong at 22 euros on 11 May 2026, and finally, on 16 July 2026, a binding, non-withdrawable promise to tender the residual 16.8% into Uber's cash takeover offer at 41.50 euros a share - roughly double what Prosus accepted three months earlier and about 2.8 times Delivery Hero's 52-week low of 14.80 euros. The forced seller is finished, and it sold at premiums rather than into a fire sale. What is left is the real security, and it is cheap on the company's own numbers. Prosus publishes its asset value daily; as of 24 July 2026 it stands at 147.2 billion US dollars, or 61.30 euros per share, against a 37.85-euro price - a 38% discount. Roughly 47.40 euros per share of that is a single liquid holding, about 22.8% of Tencent, the Chinese internet group, so a buyer at 37.85 euros pays 0.80 times the value of the Tencent stake alone and collects the 32.8 billion dollars of unlisted businesses and 7.3 billion dollars of other listed holdings for nothing. Meanwhile the company retires its own stock relentlessly - about 42 billion dollars returned since June 2022, roughly 30% of the free float, with a further 5 billion dollars committed on 29 June 2026 - which lifts value per share by arithmetic every day the discount stays wide (management puts the cumulative gain at 18%). The operating businesses have stopped being a drag: the year to 31 March 2026 delivered about 12% revenue growth, ecosystem adjusted operating earnings up roughly 44%, free cash flow above 1.5 billion dollars, and profitability across all three regional ecosystems for the first time. If Tencent merely steadies and the discount narrows toward 25%, the shares are worth about 46 euros; on a Tencent recovery toward its 200-day average with a 30% discount, closer to 50. Morgan Stanley, upgrading the stock on 25 March 2026, set a 51-euro target on the argument that the discount had reached the top of its range.
bear_thesis: The bear case has two parts, and the first is fatal to the reason this name sits in an event-driven book at all. The forced selling was in Delivery Hero shares, not in Prosus shares, so there was never a supply overhang on this security to clear - and the residual position is far too small to move the price in any case. Delivery Hero has roughly 304 million shares; the 16.8% Prosus still owns is about 51 million shares, worth about 2.1 billion euros at the 41.50-euro offer. Spread across roughly 2.11 billion Prosus shares, the entire remaining holding is worth about 1.00 euro per Prosus share - about 2.6% of the price and 1.6% of asset value. The part not yet earned, the gap between Delivery Hero's 37.90 euros today and the 41.50 offer, is worth about 0.09 euro per Prosus share, and it does not arrive until the second half of 2027, subject to merger-control and financial-regulatory clearances and to Germany's financial regulator first approving the offer document. A quarter of one percent of the share price, more than a year out, with regulatory conditions attached, is not a special situation. Second, and more seriously, the thing that actually moves this security has no floor under it. About three-quarters of the value is one Chinese equity. Tencent trades at HK$443 against a 52-week high of HK$683, down about 35%, below both its 50-day (about HK$449) and 200-day (about HK$539) averages, pressured by worries about gaming revenue and money rotating out of Chinese internet names into artificial-intelligence trades. Prosus has followed: 37.85 euros against a 52-week high of 63.94, with a 52-week low of 36.17 set within the past week. The floor our board recorded, 37.365, has already been traded through - a level the security has already broken is not a floor, it is a recent price. There is no tender, no cash consideration, no deal price obliging anyone to pay a number here; the support is a mark-to-market on a volatile foreign equity. If Tencent falls another 13-15%, roughly 7 euros a share of value disappears and Prosus can trade to the low 30s without the discount widening at all. The holding-company discount itself is structural and has never durably closed, and the street cannot even agree it is wide: Morgan Stanley upgraded four months ago because the discount was at the top of its range, while Goldman Sachs initiated at neutral on 4 June 2026 with a 41-euro target calling the discount 30% against a 40% historical average - narrow, not wide. Goldman's specific concern also bites: weaker cash flow from the operating businesses could force Prosus to keep selling Tencent shares to fund the buyback, shrinking future value per share. There is also a small negative option outstanding: the European Commission's compliance deadline is 11 October 2026 while the Uber deal does not close until the second half of 2027, and it is not yet formally established that Brussels accepts a 2027 settlement as satisfying a 2026 obligation.
sop_bull: About 46 to 50 euros per share. Start from the company's own published asset value on 24 July 2026: a 153.9 billion dollar portfolio less 6.8 billion dollars of net debt equals 147.2 billion dollars, or 61.30 euros per share on roughly 2.11 billion shares. The bull path does not require a higher mark on the parts - it requires the gap between price and parts to close part-way. Two levers: Tencent recovering from HK$443 toward its 200-day average near HK$539 lifts asset value per share to roughly 70 euros, and the discount narrowing from 38% toward the 25-30% that prevailed before this year's China selloff. At 61.30 euros of value and a 25% discount the shares are worth about 46 euros; on a Tencent recovery with a 30% discount, about 49 to 50. The buyback adds independently: 5 billion dollars a year of repurchase at a 38% discount adds roughly 3-4% to value per share annually. Morgan Stanley's 51-euro target (25 March 2026) sits just above this range. The Delivery Hero resolution contributes about 0.09 euro of unearned spread - immaterial, and deliberately not leaned on.
sop_bear: About 32 euros per share, and the honest answer is that this is a modelled bear value, not a verified floor. The parts, per the company's 24 July 2026 disclosure: Tencent 113.8 billion dollars (about 47.40 euros per share), other listed holdings 7.3 billion (about 3.00 euros), unlisted businesses 32.8 billion (about 13.70 euros), less 6.8 billion dollars of net debt (about 2.80 euros). The adverse case marks Tencent down about 13% to the high HK$300s - a retest of levels within this drawdown rather than a crisis assumption - and haircuts the unlisted book by a fifth for the same emerging-market risk aversion. That takes value per share to roughly 54 to 55 euros, and holding the discount at its current wide 38-40% gives about 32 to 33 euros. The first waypoint on the way is the 52-week low of 36.17 euros set in the past week. Nothing contractual arrests the decline: there is no cash tender, no deal price, no net-cash backstop - net debt is 6.8 billion dollars, small at about 4% of the portfolio but still a liability rather than a cushion. The only genuine hard support is that Tencent alone is marked at 47.40 euros per share, so a buyer at 37.85 euros already owns the rest for free; that is asset backing, and it moves with the tape.
sop_fair_value: About 41 euros per share, probability-weighted; the parts themselves are worth 61.30 euros per share (Prosus's own published figure, 24 July 2026) and the gap is the persistent holding-company discount.
sop_breakdown: Per Prosus share, on roughly 2.11 billion shares and the company's 24 July 2026 disclosure (147.2 billion dollars equals 129.5 billion euros, so about 1.137 dollars to the euro): Tencent, about 22.8% of the Chinese internet group, 113.8 billion dollars, about 47.40 euros - roughly 74% of gross value. Other listed holdings 7.3 billion dollars, about 3.00 euros, and this is where the entire remaining Delivery Hero position sits, worth about 1.00 euro per share at Uber's 41.50-euro offer. Unlisted businesses 32.8 billion dollars, about 13.70 euros, spread across Europe, Latin America, India and other. Less net debt of 6.8 billion dollars, about 2.80 euros. Gross portfolio 153.9 billion dollars, net asset value 147.2 billion dollars, 61.30 euros per share. Reconciling to a base case: a 25% chance the discount narrows toward 25% and Tencent steadies, worth about 47 euros; a 55% chance the status quo holds - the discount stuck near 38%, Tencent drifting, the buyback adding 3-4% a year to value per share - worth about 40 to 41 euros; a 20% chance Tencent retests the high HK$300s and the discount stays wide, worth about 32 euros. Weighted, about 41 euros against a 37.85-euro price.
risk_reward: Roughly 1.4 to 1, and the risk is undefined. Upside to a 46-euro target is about +22%; downside to a 32-euro bear value is about -15%. Our board recorded 2.76 to 1, but that was computed from a live price of 39.72 and a floor of 37.365 - and the shares have since traded to 36.17, so the floor input is broken and the ratio it produced is not real. More important than the arithmetic: on a genuine defined-risk special situation the downside is bounded by something contractual. Here it is bounded by nothing - the support is a daily mark on a Chinese equity that is 35% below its 52-week high and has not turned - so the true loss distribution has a long left tail the ratio does not capture.
catalyst_summary: The regulator-mandated Delivery Hero sell-down is finished and was never large enough to matter: Prosus cut 26.5% to 16.8% at premiums (20 euros to Uber on 17 April, 22 euros to Aspex on 11 May 2026) and on 16 July 2026 gave a binding promise to tender the rest into Uber's 41.50-euro cash offer, leaving about 0.09 euro per Prosus share of unearned spread that does not settle until the second half of 2027 - against a security whose price is set, three-quarters of it, by Tencent.
dated_milestone: Two dates remain, neither of which forces a re-rating in this security. 11 October 2026: the European Commission's extended deadline for Prosus to have complied with its divestment commitment (the two-month extension was confirmed on 2 June 2026, after Naspers asked Brussels on 25 May 2026 to end the forced sale altogether). Prosus's stated position, from its 16 July 2026 announcement, is that the sale to Uber is a fair price and an effective way to comply; whether the Commission formally accepts a settlement that completes in 2027 against a 2026 deadline is the one genuinely open item, and its downside is a small residual placement, not a re-rating. Second half of 2027: expected completion of Uber's voluntary cash takeover offer for Delivery Hero at 41.50 euros a share, announced 16 July 2026, conditional on a minimum acceptance of 50% plus one share (Prosus's binding undertaking takes Uber to about 53% of the economics, so this is effectively pre-satisfied) and on merger-control and financial-regulatory clearances, with Germany's financial regulator required to approve the offer document before publication.
forcing_function: There is no longer one, and that is the finding. The event that was supposed to force the re-rating has resolved, and the resolution is worth about 0.09 euro per share on a 37.85-euro stock, arriving in the second half of 2027. What remains that could plausibly force a re-rating is not an event but a process: the 5 billion dollar annual buyback committed on 29 June 2026, which retires stock at a 38% discount and has already taken about 30% of the free float out since June 2022, and any move to simplify the ownership structure between Prosus and its parent Naspers. Neither has a date. The nearest thing to a hard date is 11 October 2026, and the honest reading is that it is a compliance checkpoint on 1.6% of asset value, not a trigger. Absent an event, the driver is Tencent's own tape, and Tencent's next scheduled results are the only calendar item that reliably moves this security.
consensus_delta: There is no disagreement with the market worth owning here, and pretending otherwise is where this position would go wrong. The street's view is straightforward and, as far as we can verify, correct: Prosus is a discounted way to own Tencent, the discount is wide because Chinese internet sentiment is poor, and the buyback is the main thing management controls. Morgan Stanley upgraded to overweight on 25 March 2026 with a 51-euro target, explicitly because the discount had widened to the top of its post-2022 range. That call is four months old and about 5% underwater, which is itself the useful information: the discount being wide was already the consensus reason to buy, and it has widened further. Goldman Sachs then initiated at neutral on 4 June 2026 with a 41-euro target, describing the discount as 30% against a 40% historical average - the opposite framing, from a different asset-value methodology - and warning that weaker operating cash flow could force more Tencent selling to fund the buyback. When two houses cannot agree whether the discount is wide or narrow, 'the discount is at its extreme' is not an edge, it is a methodology choice. Where our board did disagree with the market was in treating the forced Delivery Hero sale as a live supply story on this security, and that disagreement does not survive verification. The selling was in another company's shares; the position was under 2% of value; it has been sold at premiums; and the residual is contracted. If any gap remains between our view and the market's, it runs the other way - the market may still be crediting Prosus with Delivery Hero optionality that has already been converted into a fixed 41.50-euro claim settling in the second half of 2027. The one asymmetry we would defend is arithmetic rather than analytical: at 37.85 euros a buyer pays 0.80 times the marked value of the Tencent stake alone and receives about 14 euros a share of other portfolio, less debt, at no cost. That is a fact about the price, not a variant view.
valley_of_death: The next three to nine months carry real downside with no offsetting event. The dominant risk is simply Tencent: it trades at HK$443 against a 52-week high of HK$683, below both its 50-day (about HK$449) and 200-day (about HK$539) averages, pressured by concerns about gaming revenue and a rotation of money out of Chinese internet names into artificial-intelligence trades. Prosus is roughly 74% Tencent by value, so a further 15% decline there removes about 7 euros a share and would put the stock in the low 30s on an unchanged discount. Second, the discount can widen independently of the assets, and each point costs roughly 0.6 euro a share. Third, currency: the portfolio is denominated in dollars and Hong Kong dollars while the listing is in euros, so a firmer euro mechanically lowers value per share. Fourth, the 11 October 2026 compliance deadline: if Brussels declines to treat the binding promise to Uber as compliance, Prosus must place a residual Delivery Hero block into the market in the fourth quarter - immaterial to value at about 1.00 euro a share, but an unhelpful headline in a tape already looking for reasons to sell. There is no cash-burn or maturity problem: net debt is 6.8 billion dollars against a 153.9 billion dollar portfolio, roughly 4%, free cash flow was above 1.5 billion dollars in the year to March 2026, and 2027 maturities were refinanced with new bonds raised in July 2026. The near-term risk is entirely price, not solvency.
positioning_washout: The mechanical selling in this situation was never in Prosus - it was in Delivery Hero, and it is over. Prosus placed 4.5% with Uber at 20 euros and 5% with Aspex at 22 euros, both at or above the prevailing market, and has now contracted the remaining 16.8% to Uber at 41.50 euros; there is no further Prosus supply coming to the Delivery Hero tape, and Delivery Hero has re-rated from a 52-week low of 14.80 euros to 37.90 accordingly. Whatever wash-out premium existed accrued to Delivery Hero's shareholders, not to ours. On Prosus's own register the flow runs the other way and is supportive rather than distressed: the company is the dominant buyer of its own stock, having retired roughly 42 billion dollars since June 2022 - about 30% of the free float - with another 5 billion dollars committed on 29 June 2026. The genuine forced-selling risk today is exogenous: passive and emerging-market funds cutting Chinese internet exposure, which hits Tencent and Prosus together and is precisely the pressure that produced the 36.17-euro low this month. That is a headwind on the position, not a set-up to buy into.
moderator_conclusion: Pass for now - not because the company is bad, but because this is not the security the board thought it was buying. The event we underwrote has already happened, and it happened well. Prosus was ordered by Europe's competition regulator to shrink a 26.5% stake in Delivery Hero as the condition of buying Just Eat Takeaway.com, and it did so at premiums: 20 euros to Uber on 17 April 2026, 22 euros to Aspex on 11 May, and then on 16 July a binding promise to tender the residual 16.8% into Uber's 41.50-euro cash offer. The forced seller is finished. The re-rating that flowed from it went to Delivery Hero's own shareholders, whose stock went from under 15 euros to 37.90. What reaches us is about 0.09 euro per Prosus share of unearned spread, settling in the second half of 2027 subject to regulatory clearance - roughly a quarter of one percent of the share price. You cannot build a defined-risk position on that. Worse for the trade as written, the downside floor our board recorded at 37.365 has already broken: the shares touched 36.17 within the past week and traded as low as 37.27 today. A level the security has already traded through is a recent price, not a floor, and there is nothing contractual beneath it - no tender, no deal price, no net cash. What actually sets the price is Tencent, about three-quarters of value, down roughly 35% from its 52-week high on gaming-revenue worries and a rotation into artificial-intelligence trades. That is an uncapped exposure wearing a special-situation label, and it does not belong in this book. The separate question is whether the security is cheap, and the honest answer is yes. Prosus's own disclosure on 24 July 2026 puts asset value at 147.2 billion dollars, or 61.30 euros a share, against a 37.85-euro price - a 38% discount. The Tencent stake alone is marked at about 47.40 euros a share, so a buyer pays 0.80 times one liquid holding and gets 32.8 billion dollars of unlisted businesses and the rest for nothing, while the company retires 5 billion dollars a year of its own stock at that discount. The operating side has genuinely turned: about 12% revenue growth in the year to March 2026, ecosystem earnings up roughly 44%, free cash flow above 1.5 billion dollars, every ecosystem profitable. That is a real value case, and it is why the value score is a 3 rather than a 1 - there is substantial asset backing, but it marks to market on a volatile Chinese equity every day, so the margin of safety is genuine without being defined. It is held to a 3 rather than a 4 for two reasons: the street cannot agree the discount is even wide (Goldman Sachs, 4 June 2026, calls it 30% against a 40% historical average), and the buyback that does the compounding may itself have to be funded by selling the asset that provides the backing. Our judgement: this name should be handed to the value book and underwritten as a discounted holding company carrying China risk, sized for that. In the event-driven book, where the entry condition is a live, dated catalyst with a floor beneath it, it is a pass. If it is to be revisited here, the level to wait for is a Tencent stabilisation - a reclaim of its 50-day average near HK$449 - with Prosus holding above 36 euros, or a concrete move to simplify the Prosus-Naspers ownership structure, which would be the first genuine forcing event this security has had.
interrogator_dossier:
# PRX.AS — Prosus N.V. — Forensic Interrogation of the Event

*Event-driven special situation. Board label: forced seller / forced-divestment flow. Every fact below was checked against public sources on 27 July 2026.*

---

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC — what the event was, and where it actually stands

The trade our board wrote down was a supply story. Prosus, the Amsterdam-listed technology holding company, was ordered by Europe's competition regulator to shrink a large stake in Delivery Hero, the German food-delivery group. The European Commission made that sell-down a condition of letting Prosus buy Just Eat Takeaway.com, and Prosus committed to cut its 26.5% Delivery Hero holding substantially. The standard way to trade a forced seller is to wait until the seller is finished, then buy the security once the pressure on the price is gone.

The first problem is definitional, and it is fatal. The forced selling was in Delivery Hero shares, not in Prosus shares. There was never an overhang on this security to clear.

The second problem is that the seller has finished — and finished well. The verified sequence:

| Date | Event | Price / terms | Residual stake |
|---|---|---|---|
| Aug 2025 | Commission clears the Just Eat Takeaway purchase, conditional on a substantial sell-down | — | 26.5% |
| 17 Apr 2026 | 13,582,342 shares (about 4.5%) sold to Uber | €20.00 per share | 21.8% |
| 11 May 2026 | 15,188,284 shares (about 5.0%) sold to Aspex Management of Hong Kong | €22.00 per share | 16.8% |
| 25 May 2026 | Naspers, Prosus's majority owner, asks Brussels for relief | — | 16.8% |
| 2 Jun 2026 | Commission extends the compliance deadline by two months, to 11 October 2026 | — | 16.8% |
| 16 Jul 2026 | Uber launches a voluntary cash takeover offer for all of Delivery Hero; Prosus gives an irrevocable undertaking (a binding, non-withdrawable promise) to tender its entire residual holding | €41.50 per share in cash; about $14.8bn equity value; closing targeted for the second half of 2027 | 16.8%, contractually spoken for |

That is the whole arc. Two placements at premiums, then the balance handed to a strategic buyer at €41.50 — roughly double the €20 accepted three months earlier, and about 2.8 times Delivery Hero's 52-week low of €14.80. The re-rating this produced went overwhelmingly to Delivery Hero's own shareholders: their stock has moved from under €15 to €37.90, against a 200-day average of €24.61.

**The event has fired.** It did not slip and it did not stall. It resolved, and it resolved competently.

## 2. THE LOAD-BEARING TEST — is the event real, dated, binding, and does it move *this* security?

Real: yes. Dated: two dates remain. Binding: yes — and that is exactly the problem, because a binding contract at a known price is a spread, and this spread is tiny.

The two remaining dates:

- **11 October 2026** — the extended deadline by which Prosus must have complied with its divestment commitment. Prosus's stated position, from the 16 July announcement, is that Uber's offer "represents a fair price and effective way to comply with its commitments to the European Commission." Whether Brussels formally accepts a contract that settles in 2027 as satisfying a 2026 obligation is the one genuinely open item; trade-press reporting suggests the Commission is minded to treat Uber's own stake-building as justification for the delay. Either way, the downside of a negative answer is that Prosus places a small block of Delivery Hero shares with someone else — an administrative outcome, not a re-rating.
- **Second half of 2027** — expected completion of Uber's offer, subject to a minimum acceptance of 50% plus one share (Prosus's undertaking takes Uber to roughly 53% of the economics, so that condition is effectively pre-satisfied) and to merger-control and financial-regulatory clearances, with Germany's financial regulator required to approve the offer document before publication.

Now the size test, which is where the thesis dies. Delivery Hero has roughly 304 million shares; Prosus's 16.8% is about 51 million shares, worth about €2.1 billion at the €41.50 offer. Prosus has roughly 2.11 billion shares outstanding. So the **entire remaining Delivery Hero position is worth about €1.00 per Prosus share** — about 2.6% of a €37.85 share price, and 1.6% of stated asset value. The part not yet earned, the gap between Delivery Hero's €37.90 today and the €41.50 offer, is about **€0.09 per Prosus share**, and it does not settle until the second half of 2027, with regulatory conditions attached.

Roughly a quarter of one percent of the share price, more than a year out. You cannot build a defined-risk position in an €81 billion holding company on that.

## 3. WHAT ACTUALLY SETS THE PRICE

Prosus publishes its own asset value. As of **24 July 2026** it stands at $147.2 billion (€129.5 billion), or **€61.3 per share**:

| Component | Value ($bn) | Per Prosus share (€) |
|---|---|---|
| Tencent, the Chinese internet group (about 22.8% of it) | 113.8 | ~47.4 |
| Other listed holdings (this is where the Delivery Hero residual sits) | 7.3 | ~3.0 |
| Unlisted portfolio — Europe, Latin America, India, other | 32.8 | ~13.7 |
| Less net debt | (6.8) | ~(2.8) |
| **Net asset value** | **147.2** | **€61.3** |

At today's €37.85 the shares trade at roughly a **38% discount** to that figure. Put another way: the Tencent stake alone is marked at about €47.40 per Prosus share, so a buyer at €37.85 pays **0.80 times one liquid holding** and collects the $32.8 billion unlisted portfolio and the other listed assets for nothing.

Which means, to about three-quarters of its value, this security is a discounted way to own Tencent — and Tencent is why the stock is where it is. Tencent trades at HK$443 against a 52-week high of HK$683, down about 35%, below both its 50-day average (HK$449) and its 200-day (HK$539). Prosus has tracked it: €37.85 against a 52-week high of €63.94, with a 52-week low of €36.17 set within the past week, a 50-day average of €39.04 and a 200-day of €46.31. The trend is down and has not turned.

## 4. THE FLOOR — the single most important verification, and it fails

Our board recorded a downside floor of €37.365 and a recovery risk-reward of 2.76 against a live price of €39.72. Both inputs are stale and the floor has already given way: the shares traded as low as €36.17 in the past week, and today's session opened at €37.28 and low-ticked €37.27. **A level the security has already traded through is not a floor. It is a recent price.**

Is there any real floor? There is asset backing, which is a different and weaker thing:

- **What supports the price.** The Tencent stake is liquid, marked daily, and worth about €47.40 per Prosus share against a €37.85 price. Prosus is also the dominant buyer of its own stock — roughly $42 billion returned since June 2022, about 30% of the free float retired, with a further $5 billion committed on 29 June 2026. Management puts the cumulative gain in value per share at 18%. Buying back stock at a 38% discount lifts value per share by arithmetic every day the discount persists.
- **Why that is not a floor.** The support marks to market on a volatile foreign equity. If Tencent falls another 15%, roughly €7 per share of Prosus value simply disappears and the stock can trade into the low €30s with the discount unchanged. There is no cash tender, no deal price, no net-cash backstop — net debt is $6.8 billion, small at about 4% of the portfolio, but still a liability rather than a cushion. A special-situation floor is a number somebody is obliged to pay you. There is none here.

The defensible adverse case is therefore not €37.37. It is Tencent retesting the high HK$300s with the discount stuck near 38%, which puts Prosus at roughly **€32**, with the €36.17 low as the first waypoint.

## 5. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

**Concerning**

- The labelled catalyst is spent, and was never sized to matter — under 2% of asset value even before it resolved.
- The recorded floor broke this month. What sits beneath is Chinese-equity exposure, which is uncapped and unhedged in this book.
- One asset drives roughly three-quarters of the value, and its own tape is deteriorating on a fundamental worry (gaming revenue) plus money rotating out of Chinese internet names into artificial-intelligence trades.
- The holding-company discount is structural and has never durably closed. Morgan Stanley upgraded to overweight on 25 March 2026 with a €51 target, explicitly because the discount had widened to the top end of its range since the open-ended buyback began in 2022. Four months later the shares are about 5% lower and the discount is wider. Buying a wide discount is not the same as being paid for it.
- The street is genuinely split on whether the discount is even wide. Goldman Sachs initiated at neutral on 4 June 2026 with a €41 target, describing the discount as 30% against a 40% historical average — that is, narrow rather than wide. The gap between the two houses is methodology (analyst-target asset values versus traded marks), which means "the discount is at its extreme" is a contested claim, not a fact.
- Goldman's specific worry is worth carrying: weaker cash flow from the operating businesses could force Prosus to keep selling Tencent shares to fund the buyback, which shrinks future value per share.
- The residual regulatory question — whether Brussels accepts a 2027 settlement against an 11 October 2026 deadline — is a small negative option, not a positive one.

**Encouraging**

- Management executed a mandated sale about as well as one can be executed: premiums on both placements, then a strategic exit at €41.50. That is evidence about how they will handle the next forced decision.
- The operating businesses have stopped being a drag. The year to 31 March 2026 delivered about 12% revenue growth, ecosystem adjusted earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation up roughly 44%, free cash flow above $1.5 billion, and profitability across all three regional ecosystems for the first time.
- The balance sheet is conservative: $6.8 billion of net debt against a $153.9 billion portfolio, roughly 4% loan-to-value, with 2027 maturities already refinanced.
- The buyback is large, real, and self-reinforcing while the discount is wide.

## 6. HIDDEN SIGNALS

Two things are worth noticing in how this played out. First, Prosus asked Brussels on 25 May 2026 to be released from the forced sale altogether, and settled for a two-month extension instead. That is a management team that knew it was selling into a weak print and tried to avoid it — creditable, and also a reminder that the April €20 placement was a genuinely poor price relative to what arrived eight weeks later. Second, the €41.50 outcome was produced by a third party's strategic appetite, not by anything Prosus engineered. The lesson for underwriting the next mandated sale is that the good result here was substantially luck, and should not be extrapolated into a management skill premium.

## 7. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: stable. The operating businesses are improving and the capital return is disciplined, but neither changes what the security is — a discounted claim on Tencent with a portfolio attached.

The single thing the director must weigh before sizing: **this name does not belong in an event-driven book.** The event that got it here has resolved, it was never large enough to move this price, and what remains is a Chinese-internet exposure wearing a special-situation label. The value case is separately genuine — a 38% discount on the company's own numbers, liquid asset backing at 0.80 times the Tencent stake alone, and a large buyer of its own stock — but it has to be underwritten as a discounted holding company carrying China risk, sized for that, and not as a defined-risk trade with a floor, because there is no floor.

Moat is not a meaningful concept for a holding company: the operating quality sits inside Tencent and belongs to Tencent, not to Prosus. The structural risk to terminal value is Chinese regulatory and geopolitical, which is real, long-known, and manageable rather than newly deteriorating.

CREDIBILITY_SCORE: 4 | TRAJECTORY: STABLE | MOAT: NONE | MOAT_TREND: STABLE | SECULAR_THREAT: manageable
